name: Intraoral genioplasty

card.summary: A chin bone-reshaping surgery done through an incision inside the mouth, so there is no visible scar, to change chin projection or height.
card.note: Surgery with swelling, lip numbness and nerve risks; performed by oral/maxillofacial or plastic surgeons.

quick.overview:
Genioplasty reshapes the chin so it balances the rest of the face. In the intraoral approach, the surgeon works through an incision inside the lower lip, leaving no external scar.

The appearance payoff is a chin with more or less projection or height, which changes the lower-face profile. It is often done alongside rhinoplasty to balance facial proportions.[1]
quick.how: In sliding genioplasty a horseshoe-shaped segment of the lower jaw is cut and moved forward or backward and fixed with plates and screws or wires. Implants are an alternative placed through an intraoral or under-chin incision.[1] Recovery involves soft foods for a period, and wire-fixed procedures may require the jaw to be wired for about 3-4 weeks.[1]
quick.risks: Common effects are swelling, bruising and temporary lip weakness or numbness; less common are infection, bone changes, implant displacement and nerve damage, with surgeon experience reducing risk.[1]

lead: Genioplasty is surgery to augment or reduce the chin, and an intraoral approach reaches the bone through the inside of the lower lip, avoiding an external scar.[1] Looksmaxxing forums discuss it as a hardmaxxing option for chin projection and lower-face balance.

Techniques include implants, sliding genioplasty, T-osteotomy (narrowing and lengthening by about 2-3 mm) and non-surgical filler.[1] Orthognathic surgery may be needed where a small chin accompanies a bite problem.[1]
It is mainly cosmetic and is performed by oral and maxillofacial surgeons, otolaryngologists or plastic surgeons.[1]

chain: Greater or lesser projection and height
angle.text: The bone itself is moved, so the chin's shape changes permanently, with the incision hidden inside the mouth.

infobox: Soft diet; jaw wiring 3-4 weeks for wire fixation

paras: The procedure is a chin osteotomy: a segment of the lower jaw is cut and moved, then secured with plates and screws or wires.[1] Intraoral incisions leave no visible scar, and some bone procedures such as the T-osteotomy are done intraorally.[1]
Swelling, bruising and temporary lip numbness are common. Infection, bone changes, implant displacement and nerve damage are less common.[1]
